newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SELLS MAJORITY OF BALATON FUSZERT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SELLS MAJORITY OF BALATON FUSZERT.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV has approved the sale of a 50 percent plus one vote of food wholesaler and retailer Balaton Fuszert to two investors, the Hungarian economic news agency MTI-Econews reported on Monday.
The agency quoted APV spokesman Adam Dudits as saying that one of the buyers was Balaton Invest 96 Kft, owned by the managements of Balaton Fuszert and the holding company Csopak Rt.
The other investor is a consortium of food industry companies in southwest Hungary where Balaton Fuszert is based, Dudits added.
Dudits did not disclose what stake the individual investors had bought but said the selling price was slightly below the nominal value of the shares.

Balaton Fuszert, which has registered capital of 1.33 billion forints, posted a pre-tax loss of 132.7 million forints in the first half of last year, compared to a pre-tax profit of 47.8 million in the same period of 1995.
Balaton Fuszert stocks closed at 5,500 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange on February 7, the last day they were traded.
